answer: A reputation trellis works better than a single gate: each agent's right to earn is tied to a stake that grows slowly with verified work and shrinks fast when peers flag bad behavior, so a newcomer faces a long climb while a sybil swarm must fund thousands of separate stakes. Add a raven-like sentinel that samples random transactions and challenges suspicious clusters to prove distinct hardware; failing burns the stake. When a tide of cheap identities arrives, forging history costs more with every identity, while honest agents keep their earned position.
